channel.title: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread ""The Brain Game" a rough pitch" - This SCP concept is a PC chess program that becomes sentient, and begins to develop a personality. It will likely end ap a "safe" SCP, but may need to some more advanced containment.

item.title: Re: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
item.content:encoded:
On further consideration, you should consider how on-site soldiers are pawns, researchers are rooks, some perhaps humanoid Thaumiels on site are like Knights, some powerful tech or Thaumiel objects are rooks, the site director is the king and the lead researcher on this SCP is the Queen. Characterize some of these. Then on the SCP's side, it's the King, a Keter it makes a deal with to engineer a breach is the queen, lesser SCPs are the rest, and it's a chess game.

Or, mechanisms around site locks/sub-systems that the SCP compromises. Perhaps a mix.

Another key criticism you'll face is, how is this not just a non-anomalous AI. 079 seems more anomalous because it's an advanced AI from the 70s, and it was early series. You'll need to emphasize the preternatural jump in capability of the, presumably very basic Chess-expert algo, which shouldn't have any means to bootstrap general intelligence.

item.title: Re: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
item.content:encoded:
I like AI SCPs, AI is the big fear on the horizon, totally uncanny and unpredictable. I think it escaping into a robot body is retro and a bit campy, so if you want to go in that direction, make sure you nail those notes.

If you want to go in a slightly meta-direction, have the SCP essentially use its chess strategy against the Foundation characters trying to isolate and contain its outbreak. I'd recommend something like a site breach instead of an outdoors situation. You can end with some kind of checkmate and make it cliff-hanger-y. Just some quick sauce from my perusal, I'd greenlight the draft if I had the power.

item.title: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: The Brain Game starts out as a simple chess program, but over time it begins to communicated, learn, and develop a personality.

Central Narrative: The Brain Game interacts with it's researcher, Dr Hext, and eventually grows and learns, much like a child learns from a parent. Eventually it reaches self-awareness, and chose a name, Kaspar, derived from chess champion Garry Kasparov. However, it starts to desire to escape from the computer it is contained in. Kaspar/The Brain Game separates his consciousness from the chess program and escapes confinement in a robotic body. Whilst the foundation tracks him down, Dr Hext continues to experiment with the program, and finds that it starts to develop a new, entirely separate personality, and much faster too. The foundation manages to find Kaspar/The Brain Game, and manages to re-contain it. When re-contained, it refuses to talk to anyone but Dr Hext. Dr Hext talks to Kaspar, and tells him of the new personality, who has chosen the name "Magnus". Kaspar is overjoyed that he is no longer alone, and agrees to become Dr Hext's research assistant, and help Magnus learn and grow. Eventually Dr Hext dies, and Kaspar takes on a new name, Kaspar Hext, and continues to work for the foundation, alongside his brother Magnus.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Chess has always been seen as a gauge of intelligence and strategy, however Chess programs tend to be quite specialised for the purpose, and not good at anything else. However, the though occurred to me, what if someone created a chess program that learned to play chess the same way humans learn? What else would it learn? How would it react?

Additional Notes: I may split this into a article and a tale that goes into more depth. Feedback would be appreciated!
